plain: To fill fully, past the point of wanting more

webster.text: To fill; to satisfy appetite or desire; to feed to the full, or to furnish enjoyment to the extent of desire; as, to satiate appetite or sense.

example.quote: I know well that instances of political moderation may be found, and a tyrant has before now descended from the plenitude of power, satiated with dominion, or worn out with care; but there is not one instance on record in all history of a number of men voluntarily abandoning the powers of an aristocracy.
example.cite: An Old Whig VIII, Philadelphia Independent Gazetteer, Feb. 6, 1788
